subject: EXT-4 — publish governed artifact downloads on https://files.geostat.internal through the shared edge
outcome: The download hostname is live on the shared edge with its own certificate, issued by a new internal CA. The existing edge certificate and key were not modified, so no client that trusts the current boundary lost trust. Signed downloads return 200 with the expected checksum; unsigned, tampered and non-GET requests are refused.

design.decision: internal CA + a dedicated leaf for the download hostname (lead decision: options 2+3 combined)
design.rationale: Re-issuing the shared self-signed certificate to add a SAN is not transparent: OpenSSL-based clients accept a self-issued certificate only when that exact certificate is in their truststore. A separate leaf under a distributed CA leaves the existing anchor untouched and makes every future hostname a leaf issuance instead of a trust migration.
design.keyType: EC P-256 for both CA and leaf. TLS 1.2 is the configured floor and every client in scope (OpenSSL 3.0, curl, JVM 17, current browsers) supports P-256; it gives smaller handshakes and cheaper signatures than RSA 3072 at equivalent strength. The script exposes --key-type rsa --rsa-bits for a client that ever needs RSA.

untouched.publicTruststore: edge/tls/public-truststore.p12 not rebuilt; its content did not have to change

history.note: kept because it is the reason for the design; the first attempt followed the original brief and was stopped at its own proof gate
history.attempt: re-issue the deployed self-signed certificate with the same key and subject, SAN + DNS:files.geostat.internal
history.result: FAIL — 'CN = geostat.internal / error 18 at 0 depth lookup: self-signed certificate'; identical with -partial_chain and -trusted
history.cause: OpenSSL treats a self-issued certificate (subject == issuer, AKI == SKI) as a root and accepts it only if that exact certificate is in the truststore; it never chains a re-issued self-signed leaf to a differently-encoded trusted copy, even though the signature verifies.

realClients.curl --cacert <old tls.crt>: curl: (60) SSL certificate problem: self-signed certificate (exit 60)
realClients.java 17, -Djavax.net.ssl.trustStore=<edg: HTTP 200 — JVM PKIX DOES accept the re-issued certificate

history.consequence: a swap would have kept the JVM services working while silently breaking every curl/browser/Go client holding the current certificate — exactly the clients EXT-4 serves. Nothing was installed; the candidate certificate and its scratch directory were deleted.
